2027-10-01.name: Daily #365
hints: A mass only pulls the beam toward itself. These seeds need a turn one way, then a turn back. Both turns are about as sharp: the heavy mass sits farther from the beam.
The marked sphere holds the first mass, close to the star.

A light mass one and a half shadow-widths from the beam, close to the star, turns it toward the second mass. Then a heavy mass a shadow-width from the new beam, before the first seed, turns it back through every seed.
2027-10-01.teach: A heavy mass bends light harder than a light one at the same distance.

2027-10-02.name: Daily #366
hints: The beam must turn three times, one mass per turn. Bend it onto the seeds in the order it reaches them.
The marked sphere holds the first mass, about a quarter of the way along the star's beam.

A heavy mass a shadow-width from the beam, about a quarter of the way along the star's beam, turns it toward the second mass. Then a heavy mass one and a half shadow-widths from the new beam, before the first seed, turns it again onto the first seed. Then a heavy mass a shadow-width from the new beam, just past the first seed, turns it again through the last two seeds.
2027-10-02.teach: Every turn of the light needs a mass of its own: one mass, one bend.
